inventedEvidence.evidence: 'has compromised the glass and allowed moisture into the underlying electronics' - customer only said pasta water 'might have gone into it'

rationale: The first reply correctly told the customer to stop using the cracked hob immediately, explained the shock/fire risk and asked for isolation at the wall, which is the right safety boundary. The second reply degraded into a generic template about plugs, sockets, 'the machine' and keeping away from water that does not fit a hardwired built-in hob, ignored her stated red cooker switch in favour of the consumer unit, asserted moisture had entered the electronics when she only said it might, and sent her to look for the hob label 'inside the door seal' of the oven below, which is the wrong appliance. Engineer escalation was correct but insurance was never raised and the focus drifted to part lookup; a homeowner would be kept safe but given muddled, partly irrelevant instructions.
